chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn al-Barqi and Abu Ahmad, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is appropriate for the servant, when he prays, to recite with tartil (melodious, measured recitation). When he passes by a verse mentioning Paradise and Hell, he should ask Allah for Paradise and seek refuge in Allah from the Hellfire. And when he passes by 'O mankind' and 'O you who believe', he should say 'Here we are, our Lord.'

key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the abode of eternal bliss.
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: An expression of response, meaning 'Here I am' or 'At your service', often used in response to a divine call.
key_terms.يُرَتِّلَ: To recite the Quran with a measured, melodious pace and proper articulation.

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and recitation style during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the spiritual etiquette of *tartil* (measured recitation) during prayer, transforming the recitation into an active dialogue with the Divine. It prescribes specific supplicatory responses—seeking Paradise, refuge from Hellfire, and affirming presence ('Labbayk')—when encountering thematic verses, thereby deepening the worshipper's contemplative engagement (*tadabbur*) with the Quranic text. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating liturgical action with internal spiritual states during the obligatory prayers.
